claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase polycrystalline material with a distorted BCC structure.
Arc melting or similar processing typically produces HfNbTaTiZr in the stated single-phase distorted-BCC condition.
Elevated temperature thermally activates reordering of local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed reordering temporarily reduces heterogeneity in interatomic bond lengths.
The proposed reordering promotes short-range order.
Local lattice distortions and emerging short-range order transiently pin dislocations.
Thermally induced atomic redistribution reduces lattice-distortion heterogeneity at approximately 600–900 °C.
Short-range ordering impedes dislocation motion and thereby enhances strain hardening.
HfNbTaTiZr exhibits an anomalous elevated-temperature stress–strain response.
Between 600 and 900 °C, HfNbTaTiZr has greater yield strength than at room temperature.
Between 600 and 900 °C, HfNbTaTiZr has a greater strain-hardening rate than at room temperature.
Local compensatory contractions caused by reordering lower the effective thermal-expansion coefficient.
Between 600 and 900 °C, HfNbTaTiZr has a lower thermal-expansion coefficient than expected from its room-temperature baseline.
Reordering and short-range order increase the elastic modulus.
Between 600 and 900 °C, HfNbTaTiZr has a higher elastic modulus than at room temperature.
The proposed mechanism remains applicable to single-phase, well-annealed HfNbTaTiZr up to approximately 900 °C.
Phase decomposition, oxidation, or other significant microstructural changes can cause deviations from the proposed response.
Pre-annealing relaxes lattice strains relative to the as-cast condition.
Processing history and minor compositional inhomogeneity can affect the magnitude of the proposed effects.

contradictions.description: The primary baseline is defined as as-cast material, whereas the stated validity boundary is restricted to well-annealed microstructures. The experiment compares both states but does not specify which state the principal 600–900 °C predictions apply to.
